A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Hsp27 is a novel tumor-derived factor that may be involved in the immunoregulation of the HBTM.
the HBTM is a unique immunosuppressive milieu that can be exploited by breast tumor cells to support their progression.

human primary breast tumors can release extremely elevated levels of Hsp 27, a known immunoregulator, which can help tumor progression by inducing differentiation of monocytes into tolerogenic macrophage that may suppress host antitumor immune responses while simultaneously promoting tumor growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the elevated expression of Hsp27 in breast tumors and its release into the tumor microenvironment may contribute to breast cancer progression by supporting tumor angiogenesis and by inducing immunotolerance.
the HBTM contains elevated levels of Hsp 27, a protein that is highly immunoregulatory.
